source.title: Low-Rank Adapting Models for Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Matthew Chen; Joshua Engels; Max Tegmark

record.tranche_reason: Reports sparse-probing evaluations of SAE latents in a real language model, bearing on whether an SAE dictionary can recover task-relevant features; it does not reproduce the original toy-model geometry experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper uses a frozen TopK SAE while adapting the language model with LoRA. The sparse-probing results directly evaluate task-feature information in SAE latents and bear on V4. The cross-entropy, steering, general-capability, and other SAE benchmark results concern the adaptation method or adjacent feature-quality measures, not the claim versions recorded here.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper. It freezes a trained SAE, fine-tunes the language model with LoRA to fit it, and reports how its own method performs: CE loss gap, speed versus e2e SAEs, SAEBench, steering and MMLU. The sparse-probing numbers (Table 6) compare the LoRA-adapted model with the unadapted model on the same SAE. They do not test whether sparse features exist in the model or are recoverable by a dictionary: there is no neuron-basis or random-dictionary control, and no superposition measure. The SAE is a tool, so none of V1–V6 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that LoRA-adapting the model around a frozen SAE reduces the SAE-inserted CE loss gap by 30–55%. They report it reaches e2e-SAE loss levels 2–20× faster, improves downstream SAE metrics and steering, and does not harm general capabilities. They argue interpretability can be improved by modifying the model, not only by post-hoc decomposition.
record.recipe_differences: The cited Toy Models of Superposition work studies feature geometry in toy networks; this paper adapts pretrained language models around frozen SAEs and evaluates downstream losses and SAE metrics.
record.method_sensitivity: Sparse-probing scores vary with the number of selected SAE latents (Top 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, or Test).

fits_no_version.finding: LoRA fine-tuning of the model around a frozen SAE closes 30–55% of the CE loss gap from inserting the SAE. It also slightly raises SAEBench scores (SCR, TPP, sparse probing) while leaving AutoInterp and absorption essentially unchanged.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A model can be cheaply adapted so that a fixed SAE dictionary becomes a more faithful account of its computation.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The relevant sparse-probing results are limited to one SAE/model setting and do not directly establish the completeness or canonical status of the learned features. The paper does not report uncertainty for the Table 6 sparse-probing scores.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were retained: the remaining reported results concern LoRA adaptation performance, general capabilities, steering, or SAE metrics that do not directly measure the claim versions.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, no geometry, no sparsity transition.
All: no analysis of capacity or feature importance.
Sparse probing uses SAE latents only, with no neuron-basis or random control. Whether features are spread across neurons, or whether the SAE recovers genuine sparse features, is not tested.
Completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features are not tested. The CE gap is treated as an engineering target.
Linearity of features is only cited (LRH, Engels et al.), not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T3' and its V4 'supports' label are not justified. A high sparse-probing score for both the base and LoRA models is a property of the SAE, which the paper does not evaluate against any control. The paper's comparison is LoRA versus no LoRA, which is its own method against a baseline.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network superposition, overlapping directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether polysemanticity results from limited capacity or feature importance.
Whether polysemanticity arises from mechanisms other than capacity pressure.

Tests sparse-probe performance on SAE latents for one Gemma-2-2B TopK SAE; does not test feature distribution across neurons or establish that SAE features are a complete account of model representations.
Completeness, stability, or canonical status of SAE features.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated sparse probing on SAE latents with the model low-rank adapted at rank 64.
rows.note: Sparse probing is described as testing how well SAE latents capture target features.
rows.check: Compares the study's own method (LoRA model 0.760) with its unadapted baseline (0.732) on the same SAE. This is method performance, not a measure of whether the dictionary recovers model features. 'Observed' has no version effect to refer to.
